chapter: Portraits from Hemphill to Getz, and the bebop question
title: Ballroom circuit: major cities, lodging arranged, mixed audiences
summary: Archer's ballrooms were in larger towns, lodging was arranged for Fletcher's band, and audiences were both black and white.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: In Nebraska and Iowa and so on did you have any -- well, let's see, did you do one nighters in smaller towns, or was it like mostly in Omaha and Des Moines, Lincoln?

During this time Fletcher was contracted to Tom Archer, and he bought the 15 days, and they only had these ballrooms in the larger towns. They were kind of few and far between, you know, but they were great ballrooms. And the lodging facilities were great. They took care
When you got in town, you knew where you were going to stay, you knew where you were going -- that was no problem. You see, he was that big an attraction to demand then.
Were these white audiences or black or both?
